targets.public_description: Package-authored Lean formalization of the converse that arXiv:2608.13599v2 proposes in section 9 (the paragraph after Question 9.1): for both-large removals, a tight two-swap speed set must satisfy the replacement conditions of Theorem 5.1, with inserted speeds at least n and the gcd interval condition (4). The formalization states it for either matching of the two replacements. It is an open proposal of that paper, not one of its theorems.
targets.reason: The relabelling gate closes on the primary check: the source itself proposes this converse, and the staged statement matches either pair assignment.

targets.public_description: Package-authored Lean formalization of the four-speed case that Fan and Sun leave open (arXiv:2306.10417v2, Conjecture 1.3 and section 6.2(1)): for a primitive set of four speeds whose pairwise gcds are at most 2, the maximum loneliness is at least 1/4 or equals s/(4s + k) for some 1 <= k <= 4 with k <= s. The condition k <= s follows from the known four-speed bound ML >= 1/5 by a kernel-checked numeric argument, so it adds nothing to the open question.
targets.reason: The hypothesis-justification gate closes on the kernel-checked numeric bridge (evidence/LonelyRunnerSpectrumBoundBridge.lean, standard axioms only) and the primary pointers.

targets.public_description: Package-authored Lean formalization of Question 6.6 of arXiv:2609.03444 (v1; the catalog cites v2, section 6.4): on near-tight six-speed sets whose maximum loneliness is p/q < 1/6 in lowest terms, is every speed below 3q? The statement requires the speed set to be primitive (no common factor). Scaling a speed set by c keeps its loneliness and q but multiplies every speed by c, so without primitivity the literal question fails for trivial reasons; primitivity is the standard normalization, not an added restriction on the open content.
targets.reason: The primitivity condition is already in the statement; the gate closes with the public description above. A Lean docstring update waits for the next source revision.

targets.public_description: Package-authored Lean formalization: every finite tree with exactly two branch vertices, of degrees 4 and 3 (so five leaves), is graceful. Panpa, Imnang and Wasuanankul (J. Appl. Math. 2025, doi:10.1155/jama/5826777) classify five-leaf trees by branch degrees (5), (4,3) and (3,3,3), prove the spider case (Theorem 3.4), and leave this family open in section 4 (Figure 10).
targets.reason: A dated primary-source screen (the source paper and arXiv:2605.14295, 2605.02303, 2608.23881) and the catalog and 307-row corpus screens found no proof of this family. Bounded screen, not a novelty guarantee.
